entral.name: ENTRAL
entral.definition: Single governing intelligence and central command layer.

marshals.name: Product and Fulfillment Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls how products are sourced, produced, customized, stocked, fulfilled, recovered, and delivered.

marshals.name: Digital and Software Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls software, data, digital content, access products, licensing, and technology-enabled delivery.

marshals.name: Marketplace Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls businesses that connect multiple participant groups and govern discovery, matching, trust, transactions, and marketplace liquidity.

marshals.name: Customer-Relationship Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls buyer and seller identity, contract structure, buying process, account ownership, and relationship economics.

marshals.name: Revenue Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls how value is priced, charged, collected, shared, renewed, and measured across businesses.

marshals.name: Service-Based E-Commerce Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls the sale, scheduling, delivery, quality, and fulfillment of services through digital commerce systems.

marshals.name: Sales-Channel Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls where and how customers discover, evaluate, buy, and receive offers across channels and interfaces.

marshals.name: Specialized Commerce Marshal
marshals.definition: Controls specialized commercial formats whose operating mechanics, customer expectations, or mission require distinct governance.

generals.name: Dropshipping General
generals.definition: Supplier-held inventory is sold by the business and shipped directly to the customer.

generals.name: Print-on-Demand General
generals.definition: Products are produced and fulfilled after purchase using customer-selected or brand-created designs.

generals.name: Private Label General
generals.definition: Contract-manufactured products are sold under a proprietary brand with controlled positioning and specifications.

generals.name: White Label General
generals.definition: Existing products are rebranded for resale with limited changes to the underlying product.

generals.name: Wholesale General
generals.definition: Goods are bought or sold in bulk, typically with account-based pricing and distribution operations.

generals.name: Direct-to-Consumer General
generals.definition: A brand sells directly to end customers without relying on traditional retail intermediaries.

generals.name: Manufacturing General
generals.definition: The business controls in-house or contracted production, quality, capacity, and supply planning.

generals.name: Handmade General
generals.definition: Artisan or craft products are produced manually in small batches or as individual pieces.

generals.name: Made-to-Order General
generals.definition: Production starts only after an order is confirmed, reducing finished-goods inventory.

generals.name: Retail Arbitrage General
generals.definition: Discounted products are sourced from physical retail locations and resold at a margin.

generals.name: Online Arbitrage General
generals.definition: Discounted products are sourced online and resold through another channel or marketplace.

generals.name: Liquidation Resale General
generals.definition: Overstock, returns, closeouts, and distressed inventory are acquired and resold.

generals.name: Refurbished Goods General
generals.definition: Used or defective goods are restored, tested, graded, warranted, and resold.

generals.name: Recommerce General
generals.definition: Previously owned products are acquired, listed, authenticated where needed, and resold.

generals.name: Consignment General
generals.definition: Products are sold on behalf of owners, with proceeds divided under an agreed revenue share.

generals.name: Subscription Boxes General
generals.definition: Curated physical products are assembled and delivered on a recurring schedule.

generals.name: Rental Commerce General
generals.definition: Customers pay for temporary access to physical products while the business retains ownership.

generals.name: Preorder Commerce General
generals.definition: Orders and often payment are accepted before inventory or production is ready.

generals.name: Crowdfunding Commerce General
generals.definition: Demand and funding are secured through campaign-backed commitments before full-scale delivery.

generals.name: Digital Downloads General
generals.definition: Files are sold and delivered electronically with no physical fulfillment requirement.

generals.name: Personalized Products General
generals.definition: Standard products are tailored with customer-specific names, images, dates, or selections.

generals.name: Custom Products General
generals.definition: Products are designed or manufactured to unique customer specifications beyond standard personalization.

generals.name: SaaS General
generals.definition: Subscription or contract access to centrally hosted software delivered over the internet.

generals.name: Micro-SaaS General
generals.definition: A narrowly scoped software product serving a specific workflow, audience, or integration need.

generals.name: Platform-as-a-Service General
generals.definition: Hosted infrastructure and development capabilities are provided for building and deploying applications.

generals.name: API-as-a-Service General
generals.definition: Programmatic capabilities are packaged and monetized through documented application interfaces.

generals.name: Data-as-a-Service General
generals.definition: Curated, processed, or continuously updated data is delivered through files, dashboards, or APIs.

generals.name: Mobile App Commerce General
generals.definition: Products, services, or paid functionality are sold primarily through a mobile application.

generals.name: Digital Products General
generals.definition: Non-physical assets such as guides, systems, media, datasets, or files are sold electronically.

generals.name: Online Courses General
generals.definition: Structured educational content, exercises, assessments, and support are sold online.

generals.name: Digital Memberships General
generals.definition: Recurring paid access is granted to digital resources, benefits, tools, or content libraries.

generals.name: Paid Communities General
generals.definition: Members pay for access to a moderated network, peer interaction, events, and shared resources.

generals.name: Paid Newsletters General
generals.definition: Subscribers pay for recurring written analysis, reporting, curation, or specialized insight.

generals.name: Software Licensing General
generals.definition: Software usage rights are sold under defined terms, seats, devices, territories, or time periods.

generals.name: Template Stores General
generals.definition: Reusable documents, designs, workflows, prompts, or system templates are sold digitally.

generals.name: Stock-Asset Stores General
generals.definition: Licensed photos, video, audio, graphics, fonts, or similar creative assets are sold from a catalog.

generals.name: Game-Asset Stores General
generals.definition: Game-ready models, textures, code, audio, maps, or systems are sold to developers.

generals.name: Plugin Stores General
generals.definition: Extensions, add-ons, integrations, themes, or modules are sold for host platforms.

generals.name: AI-as-a-Service General
generals.definition: AI capabilities are delivered as hosted applications, agents, workflows, models, or APIs.

generals.name: Online Marketplace General
generals.definition: A digital venue connects buyers and sellers and supports discovery and transactions.

generals.name: Multi-Vendor Marketplace General
generals.definition: Multiple independent vendors operate storefronts or catalogs within one platform.

generals.name: Managed Marketplace General
generals.definition: The platform actively controls quality, fulfillment, pricing, matching, or service standards.

generals.name: Peer-to-Peer Marketplace General
generals.definition: Individuals transact directly with other individuals through platform-provided trust and payment systems.

generals.name: Service Marketplace General
generals.definition: Customers discover, compare, book, and pay independent service providers.

generals.name: Freelancer Marketplace General
generals.definition: Businesses or individuals source and contract independent professional talent.

generals.name: Rental Marketplace General
generals.definition: Owners list assets for temporary use by renters while the platform manages matching and trust.

generals.name: Auction Marketplace General
generals.definition: Sellers accept competing bids and the highest qualifying bid wins under defined rules.

generals.name: Reverse-Auction Marketplace General
generals.definition: Buyers post demand and suppliers compete by offering lower prices or stronger terms.

generals.name: Classified Marketplace General
generals.definition: Users publish listings and negotiate transactions, often with limited platform involvement.

generals.name: Wholesale Marketplace General
generals.definition: Business buyers and suppliers transact in bulk with trade pricing, terms, and account controls.

generals.name: Digital-Product Marketplace General
generals.definition: Multiple creators or vendors sell downloadable or access-based digital products.

generals.name: Aggregator General
generals.definition: Offers from multiple providers are collected and presented through a unified discovery or purchasing layer.

generals.name: Comparison Marketplace General
generals.definition: Alternatives are normalized and compared by price, features, availability, or suitability.

generals.name: Two-Sided Marketplace General
generals.definition: The business creates value by attracting, matching, and retaining two interdependent participant groups.

generals.name: B2C General
generals.definition: Businesses sell products or services directly to individual consumers.

generals.name: B2B General
generals.definition: Businesses sell to other businesses through accounts, contracts, procurement, or repeat commercial relationships.

generals.name: C2C General
generals.definition: Consumers sell or exchange value with other consumers, usually through a facilitating platform.

generals.name: C2B General
generals.definition: Individuals provide products, services, data, influence, or value to businesses.

generals.name: D2C General
generals.definition: Brands own the direct relationship, transaction, and customer data for end-consumer sales.

generals.name: B2G General
generals.definition: Businesses sell to government entities under public procurement, compliance, and contracting requirements.

generals.name: G2B General
generals.definition: Government entities deliver paid or transactional services, licenses, data, or resources to businesses.

generals.name: B2B2C General
generals.definition: One business reaches end consumers through another business while responsibilities and economics are shared.

generals.name: Peer-to-Peer General
generals.definition: Participants of comparable standing exchange value directly under a trust or coordination system.

generals.name: Enterprise E-Commerce General
generals.definition: Complex organizations buy through negotiated contracts, approvals, integrations, security, and account controls.

generals.name: One-Time Purchase General
generals.definition: The customer pays once for a product, service, entitlement, or completed transaction.

generals.name: Subscription Commerce General
generals.definition: Customers pay on a recurring schedule for continued products, access, or service.

generals.name: Membership Commerce General
generals.definition: Recurring payment grants status, privileges, benefits, community access, or preferred economics.

generals.name: Freemium General
generals.definition: A free core offer drives adoption while premium capabilities or limits generate revenue.

generals.name: Usage-Based Pricing General
generals.definition: Charges vary according to metered consumption such as volume, time, calls, storage, or output.

generals.name: Transaction-Fee Model General
generals.definition: A fee is charged for each processed transaction or payment event.

generals.name: Commission Model General
generals.definition: Revenue is earned as a percentage or share of another party's sale.

generals.name: Licensing Model General
generals.definition: Customers pay for defined rights to use intellectual property, software, content, or technology.

generals.name: Affiliate Commerce General
generals.definition: Revenue is earned for attributable referrals that result in qualified actions or purchases.

generals.name: Advertising-Supported Commerce General
generals.definition: User attention or inventory is monetized through paid advertising placements.

generals.name: Sponsorship Commerce General
generals.definition: A sponsor pays to associate with content, audiences, events, products, or outcomes.

generals.name: Lead-Generation Commerce General
generals.definition: Qualified prospect information or introductions are sold to businesses.

generals.name: Pay-per-Download General
generals.definition: A separate charge is collected for each downloaded file or licensed asset.

generals.name: Pay-per-Use General
generals.definition: The customer pays each time a service, unit, feature, or asset is used.

generals.name: Recurring Replenishment General
generals.definition: Consumable products are automatically reordered and delivered at a recurring interval.

generals.name: Bundled Commerce General
generals.definition: Multiple products, services, or entitlements are packaged and priced as one offer.

generals.name: Service Commerce General
generals.definition: Services are packaged, sold, paid for, and managed through an online transaction flow.

generals.name: Booking Commerce General
generals.definition: Customers reserve time, capacity, inventory, or experiences through a booking system.

generals.name: Appointment Commerce General
generals.definition: Customers schedule time with a specific provider, professional, or location.

generals.name: On-Demand Services General
generals.definition: Services are requested and dispatched with minimal delay based on real-time availability.

generals.name: Productized Services General
generals.definition: A service is standardized into a defined scope, price, process, and deliverable.

generals.name: Consulting Commerce General
generals.definition: Expert diagnosis, strategy, or implementation guidance is sold through engagements or packages.

generals.name: Coaching Commerce General
generals.definition: Goal-oriented guidance, accountability, and development are delivered through sessions or programs.

generals.name: Tutoring Commerce General
generals.definition: Instruction and learning support are sold by subject, session, package, or outcome.

generals.name: Telehealth Commerce General
generals.definition: Health-related consultations or services are delivered remotely under applicable clinical and legal controls.

generals.name: Ticketing Commerce General
generals.definition: Access rights to events, venues, transport, or experiences are sold and validated digitally.

generals.name: Travel Booking General
generals.definition: Travel inventory and related services are searched, reserved, packaged, and paid for online.

generals.name: Food Delivery General
generals.definition: Prepared food orders are routed from merchants to customers through pickup and delivery operations.

generals.name: Local-Service Commerce General
generals.definition: Customers discover, purchase, and schedule geographically constrained services.

generals.name: Social Commerce General
generals.definition: Products are discovered and purchased within or directly through social platforms.

generals.name: Mobile Commerce General
generals.definition: The buying journey is designed primarily for smartphones, mobile web, or mobile apps.

generals.name: Live Commerce General
generals.definition: Products are demonstrated and sold during interactive live video broadcasts.

generals.name: Conversational Commerce General
generals.definition: Sales and service occur through chat, messaging, or AI-assisted conversations.

generals.name: Influencer Commerce General
generals.definition: Creators with established audiences drive demand, conversion, or co-branded sales.

generals.name: Creator Commerce General
generals.definition: Creators monetize owned audiences through products, services, memberships, or digital offers.

generals.name: Affiliate Storefronts General
generals.definition: Curated storefronts present third-party products and earn attributable referral revenue.

generals.name: Marketplace Selling General
generals.definition: A business sells through a third-party marketplace while managing listings, rank, fees, and platform rules.

generals.name: Omnichannel Commerce General
generals.definition: Channels share customer, inventory, order, and service context in one coordinated experience.

generals.name: Multichannel Commerce General
generals.definition: A business sells through multiple channels that may operate with separate processes or data.

generals.name: Cross-Border Commerce General
generals.definition: Products or services are sold internationally with localization, tax, customs, currency, and logistics controls.

generals.name: Local Commerce General
generals.definition: Demand, inventory, fulfillment, and customer experience are optimized for a defined geographic market.

generals.name: Voice Commerce General
generals.definition: Customers search, select, order, or manage purchases through voice interfaces.

generals.name: Embedded Commerce General
generals.definition: Purchasing capability is integrated inside another product, workflow, platform, or user experience.

generals.name: Subscription Boxes General
generals.definition: Recurring curated product assortments are managed as a specialized merchandising and retention format.

generals.name: Mystery Boxes General
generals.definition: Customers purchase an unknown or partially disclosed assortment with controlled value and disclosure rules.

generals.name: Group Buying General
generals.definition: Demand is aggregated so participants receive better pricing or access when thresholds are reached.

generals.name: Flash-Sale Commerce General
generals.definition: Inventory is offered for a short, predetermined window to create urgency and concentrated demand.

generals.name: Daily-Deal Commerce General
generals.definition: A rotating offer or limited set of offers is promoted for a defined day or period.

generals.name: Curated Commerce General
generals.definition: Assortments are selected and presented through expert judgment, taste, or audience fit.

generals.name: Niche Commerce General
generals.definition: A tightly defined audience or need is served with specialized products, language, and positioning.

generals.name: Luxury Commerce General
generals.definition: High-value products or services are sold through controlled brand, experience, trust, and exclusivity.

generals.name: Resale Commerce General
generals.definition: Previously owned products are marketed and sold as a specialized retail format.

generals.name: Circular Commerce General
generals.definition: Products and materials remain in use through resale, repair, return, refurbishment, or reuse loops.

generals.name: Sustainable Commerce General
generals.definition: Commercial decisions prioritize reduced environmental and social harm with supportable claims.

generals.name: Rental Commerce General
generals.definition: Temporary access is the core commercial proposition, with asset utilization and recovery as central controls.

generals.name: Fractional Ownership Commerce General
generals.definition: Multiple buyers acquire defined ownership interests or usage rights in a shared asset.

generals.name: Donation-Based Commerce General
generals.definition: Payments are voluntary contributions rather than conventional consideration for a purchase.

generals.name: Nonprofit Commerce General
generals.definition: Commercial activity supports a nonprofit mission and operates under nonprofit governance constraints.

generals.name: Cause-Related Commerce General
generals.definition: Purchases are linked to a stated social or environmental cause through defined contributions or campaigns.
